subject: swampTroll
pitch:
Category: Monster.
Subject: swamp troll with tusks, mohawk and bone fetishes.
Style: Blizzard/Warcraft.
reasoning:
I'm designing a swamp troll character: lanky and hunched with blue-green skin, tusks, a red-orange mohawk, bone fetish necklaces, a loincloth, and wrapped bracers on long digitigrade legs. I want to keep the module economical, aiming for a manageable size while being careful with API usage.

Now I'm planning the skeleton structure: hips, spine chain curving into chest and neck, head and jaw joints aimed forward, bent legs with forward knee direction, and long arms reaching down toward the knees with shoulders and wrists positioned for that hunched troll proportions.

For hands I'm thinking of a palm sphere plus finger chains built from small sweeps, wrapping that into a reusable hand-building helper. For the skin I'm setting up a paint function that mottles teal and dark green tones with noise, lightening the belly area for a countershaded effect.

Now I'm sketching the torso as a swept ellipse along the spine chain, tapering the chest radius wider at the top, and adding a separate pelvis sphere scaled for the hips. For the head I'm building a skull sphere with a brow ridge box, a large swept nose, and glowing yellow eyes made from layered spheres with black pupils positioned at the head joint coordinates.

Moving to the jaw, I'm placing a scaled sphere below the skull with upward-pointing tusk spikes jutting from either side using a spike primitive that takes a tip, a direction reference, and a length/radius.

For the muzzle, I'm adding a small sphere attached to the head bone, then shaping a hooked nose using a catmull-rom sweep path with tapering radius from base to tip.

For ears, I'm spiking outward and back from the sides of the head with angled directions for a pointed look, keeping them as simple bones without chains. Then for the mohawk, I'm planning a row of flame-like extruded blade shapes running along the crest from forehead to neck, oriented so their thickness runs along the z-axis.

Placing blades along a curved path down the head and back, with decreasing heights and alternating red/orange colors, leaning backward -- the first several attach to the head bone and the rest to the chest bone as the crest trails down the back.

I'll just approximate a few spine blade points along the back at decreasing heights with slight inward sink, keeping the hunch believable. For bone fetishes, I'm planning a necklace of small skull and bone shapes strung around the neck, plus maybe a ritual staff with a skull and feathers gripped vertically in the right hand near the wrist.

Simplifying the gripping hand into a palm sphere with finger capsules curled around the staff using arcs around its central axis.

Now I'm detailing the staff head with skull, feathers, and glowing orb, then moving to the loincloth panels with tribal paint, hip belt ring, shoulder pauldrons with bone spikes, and clawed feet with toe capsules.

Skipping the tail since trolls don't need one, and the back spikes are handled by the mohawk. I'm working out the glowing eye decals as planes positioned against the curved skull surface, calculating their exact placement using the skull's geometry, and adding a brow ridge box above them.

For textures, I'm deciding to give the eyes a yellow glow with a slit pupil, then considering whether to add tribal war paint — maybe a glyph decal placed on a plane over the chest — and a patterned loincloth texture with tribal triangles.

I'll use a decal function to project textures onto surfaces, like applying the eye texture onto the skull part and the glyph onto the torso, following the pattern from the reference example with glow applied to decals. Now I'm setting up the color palette for the skin, darker shading, and belly tones before writing the actual code.

Finishing the color constants, then defining a helper for building a simple horizontal ring of points, and writing a paint function that blends skin tones with noise for texture, lightens the top, shifts the belly color, and adds dark wart spots.

Now I'm shaping the torso with a sweep along the spine, varying its radius with sine curves to create a rounded waist that widens toward the belly and tapers near the shoulders, then moving on to sweep the neck shape.

Working out the neck chain, I'm trying to match the joint-naming pattern from the earlier yordle example—figuring out whether the number of joint names should be one less than the number of control points—and planning the head joint to parent off the last neck joint.

For legs and arms I'm similarly checking whether to follow the yordle pattern of matching names to the full count of catmull points (hip/knee/ankle for three points) rather than dropping one, since that seemed inconsistent with the neck case.

Adding feet, toes with capsule claws, and hand details...

Now I'm working out the arm chains and wrist positions, making sure the right hand's fist wraps around the staff by aligning the wrist joint with the staff's axis.

I'm building the staff as a rod bone parented to the wrist, running upward, then topping it with a skull, horns, feathers, a glowing orb, and dangling beads.

Now I'm designing a skull helper with a scaled head sphere, a jaw box, and eye socket spheres, then adding a necklace ring made from a catmull path around the chest base.

Still calculating necklace geometry...

Now I'm positioning skulls and bone fetishes around the front of the ring, then working out the belt ring at hip height and sketching the loincloth panel hanging down from it.

Now I'm working out the cloth paint pattern, mixing a gold border band with chevron stripes for the design, and considering adding a decal plane for a glyph on the front panel with a slight tilt.

For the shoulders, I'm planning leather pauldrons with bone spikes on both sides, plus bone bracer wraps on the left arm using sweep geometry. I'm also adding small character details like hair tufts, a chin braid with beads, and deciding that's enough embellishment.

Now I'm working out the hunched back and chest shape using scaled spheres, small lower jaw teeth plus large tusks, and glowing yellow-green eyes with slit pupils rendered as SVG decals mirrored across the face. I'm also sketching white facial war-paint stripes as a simple decal texture on the cheeks.

I'm placing the brow ridge sphere above the eyes, adding a chest glyph decal on the torso without a bone reference, then finishing with the default export.

Now I'm building the legs and feet: straight, hunched pose with the mohawk and staff topping out around 2.7 units, then adding toe capsules, claw spikes, and foot spheres positioned to rest just above the floor.

Writing finger chains...

I'll set the right wrist target near the arm end and position the palm slightly behind the staff so it overlaps naturally without clipping oddly. Then I'll finalize, trimming unused imports and only pulling in rng if I actually need randomized tufts or details.
